findings.claim: The new CAUTION block (lines 446-450) says the Operator 'will fail' unless the `rolling-updates` feature is enabled, but nothing in the operator checks this. Either the operator's spec.update / update strategy is not actually gated behind the preview feature, or the documentation is wrong.
findings.evidence: open-code-review and superpowers: `grep -rn "ROLLING_UPDATES\|rolling-updates" operator/src/main` finds nothing. UpgradeLogicFactory.create (UpgradeLogicFactory.java:35-43) picks the logic from UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy alone. KeycloakDistConfigurator.java:122-124 only passes spec.features through to the server. KeycloakSpec.getUpdateSpec has no validation tied to features. mattpocock: UpgradeTest.java:50 and 104-106 still expect the null-strategy path to pass without the feature. All three seats agree the UpgradeTest change (110-115) proves nothing about gating. ponytail noted the same gap but outside its role, so it is not counted. Every seat's claim is reasoned; no gate was run.
findings.reason: Accepted, with a decision needed: add a real operator gate (a status error or validation when spec.update is set without `rolling-updates`) or remove the sentence from the docs. Red test before fixing: an operator integration test that sets spec.update.strategy with no features.enabled and expects the operator to fail. On the pinned code it does not fail, so the test is red. Not yet executed (benchmark mode).

findings.claim: The patch renumbers the public exit-code contract (recreate 4 -> 3, feature-disabled = 4), but no test asserts either new value. testFeatureNotEnabled and testIncompatible check only the message text.
findings.evidence: The only exit-code assertion in the file is assertEquals(0, ...) at line 75. CompatibilityResult.java:34-35 changes the constants. The guide tells users to rely only on the exit code of `check`. The tests are @RawDistOnly, so result.exitCode() is available and meaningful. superpowers rated this Important (lines 46-50 and 88-107). mattpocock and open-code-review rated it Minor. It is normalised to Important because it guards a renumbered public contract.
findings.reason: Accepted. Add assertEquals(4, result.exitCode()) to testFeatureNotEnabled and assertEquals(3, result.exitCode()) to testIncompatible. The pinned code is believed correct, so red is shown by mutation: swapping FEATURE_DISABLED and RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE must turn the new assertions red. Not yet executed (benchmark mode).

findings.claim: Only `update-compatibility metadata` is run with the feature off. The separate copy of the gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (lines 46-50) is never run without the feature.
findings.evidence: The @Launch({UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME}) call is the only launch without ENABLE_FEATURE (superpowers). mattpocock and open-code-review make the same observation.
findings.reason: Accepted. Add a feature-off launch of `update-compatibility check` that asserts the message and exit code 4. This is Minor, so no red test is required.

findings.claim: The same 5-line feature gate (isFeatureEnabled, printFeatureDisabled, exit(FEATURE_DISABLED), return) is copied into UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java:46-50 and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java:46-50, instead of living once in AbstractUpdatesCommand.
findings.evidence: The two blocks are identical. `grep -rn printFeatureDisabled` shows only the definition (AbstractUpdatesCommand.java:83-85) and the two copies (ponytail). Any future subcommand could miss the gate (open-code-review). mattpocock lists it as a possible duplicated-code smell. findings.reason: Accepted as a small consolidation. Replace printFeatureDisabled() with one helper in AbstractUpdatesCommand, for example isRollingUpdatesDisabled(), that prints, exits and returns true. This is a net line reduction, not a speculative abstraction. Advisory and Minor, so it does not block convergence.

findings.evidence: The base docs already said 3, so this aligns code with docs. The command is unreleased (999.0.0-SNAPSHOT, added in 588e60e058) and preview. Scripts written against the old actual value 4 would now read 'feature disabled' as 'recreate'.

findings.claim: The macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` after the user's parameters. That overrides features the user enabled through KC_FEATURES or keycloak.conf, and it likely has no effect on an --optimized (pre-built) image, which would need a rebuild with the feature.
findings.evidence: This is reasoned from CLI priority and build-time option semantics, and the guide's own 'include all configuration options' rule. The branch history points the same way: b1965bb9c4 'do not use custom image, it fails', then 5d2490d33a bakes the feature into the image. Whether runtime --features applies under --optimized was not checked.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat. Listed, not reported, not fixed. The --optimized part is unverified.
